# Erdős-Nešetril Conjecture

The Erdős-Nešetril conjecture asserts that every simple graph of maximum vertex degree Image: Delta has a strong edge coloring with at most Image: 5Delta^2/4 colors (Faudree et al. 1990). A strong edge coloring partitions the edges into induced matchings, so two edges of the same color neither share a graph vertex nor have adjacent endpoints.

The coefficient Image: 5/4 cannot be reduced. Replace each graph vertex of a 5-cycle graph by an independent set of Image: t vertices and each graph edge by all edges between the corresponding sets. The resulting graph has maximum vertex degree Image: 2t and Image: 5t^2 edges, all of which must receive different colors in a strong edge coloring. The conjecture remains open (Bloom 2026).

This is problem 149 in the Erdős problems collection (Bloom 2026).

Title: The 2-Twist Spun Trefoil Has Crossing Number Six
Authors: Sherry Gong, Samuel Lewis-Monkman, Jesse Osnes
Date: Tue Jun  2 15:48:27 2026

We study the tri-plane crossing number, that is, the minimal number of crossings in a tri-plane diagram for a bridge trisection of a knotted sphere in $S^4$. We show that every 2-knot in $S^4$ that admits a bridge trisection with at most five crossings is ribbon. As a consequence, we show that the 2-twist spin of the trefoil has crossing number 6. This is the first such computation for a non-trivial knotted surface.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
